paper_title: SRPO Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware   Reinforcement Learning
caption: : Self-reflection SFT data statistic

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of sample counts across six distinct reasoning categories within the self-reflection supervised fine-tuning (SFT) dataset, as referenced in the paper “SRPO: Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware Reinforcement Learning.” The horizontal axis lists the reasoning categories — Mathematical Reasoning, General Reasoning, Natural Scene Reasoning, Physical Reasoning, Logical Puzzle Reasoning, and Chemical Reasoning — arranged in descending order of sample count. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” is presented on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10² to 10⁴, with gridlines marking each power of ten. Each bar is labeled with its exact sample count: Mathematical Reasoning has 7025 samples, General Reasoning 1709, Natural Scene Reasoning 413, Physical Reasoning 232, Logical Puzzle Reasoning 91, and Chemical Reasoning 49. The bars are uniformly colored in light blue and decrease progressively in height from left to right, visually emphasizing the skewed distribution of data, with Mathematical Reasoning dominating the dataset and Chemical Reasoning representing the smallest subset. No additional grouping, stacking, or visual highlighting is applied beyond the explicit numerical labels atop each bar.
model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart, titled “Self-reflection SFT data statistic,” visually presents the distribution of training samples across six distinct reasoning categories used in the SRPO framework for enhancing multimodal LLM reasoning. The horizontal axis lists the reasoning types—Mathematical Reasoning, General Reasoning, Natural Scene Reasoning, Physical Reasoning, Logical Puzzle Reasoning, and Chemical Reasoning—in left-to-right order, with labels rotated slightly for readability. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10² (100) to 10⁴ (10,000), with major gridlines at 10², 10³, and 10⁴, allowing for clear visualization of orders-of-magnitude differences. Each category is represented by a single light blue bar, with the exact sample count numerically labeled atop each bar: Mathematical Reasoning has 7025 samples (the highest), followed by General Reasoning with 1709, Natural Scene Reasoning with 413, Physical Reasoning with 232, Logical Puzzle Reasoning with 91, and Chemical Reasoning with 49 (the lowest). The bars are arranged in descending order of sample count from left to right, visually emphasizing the disparity in data volume across reasoning domains, with no additional visual emphasis such as shading or outlines applied to any specific bar.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of self-reflection supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data across six reasoning categories, as presented in the paper “SRPO: Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware Reinforcement Learning.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10² to 10⁴, with gridlines at 100, 1,000, and 10,000. The horizontal axis lists the reasoning categories in descending order of sample count: Mathematical Reasoning (7,025 samples), General Reasoning (1,709), Natural Scene Reasoning (413), Physical Reasoning (232), Logical Puzzle Reasoning (91), and Chemical Reasoning (49). Each category is represented by a light blue vertical bar, with the exact sample count labeled above each bar. The data shows a steep decline in sample size from Mathematical Reasoning — the most represented category — to Chemical Reasoning, which has the fewest samples. No grouping or stacking is present; each bar stands independently, and all bars are uniformly colored and styled, with no visual emphasis on any particular category beyond their height and labeled value.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm stellt die Anzahl der Proben („Number of Samples“) für verschiedene Kategorien von Selbstreflexions-SFT-Daten dar, wobei die vertikale Achse logarithmisch skaliert ist und Werte von 10² bis 10⁴ abdeckt, mit Tick-Markierungen bei 100, 1000 und 10.000. Die horizontale Achse listet sechs Kategorien in der Reihenfolge: „Mathematical Reasoning“, „General Reasoning“, „Natural Scene Reasoning“, „Physical Reasoning“, „Logical Puzzle Reasoning“ und „Chemical Reasoning“. Jeder Balken ist hellblau gefärbt und trägt seinen genauen numerischen Wert oben: „Mathematical Reasoning“ mit 7025 Proben ist der höchste Balken, gefolgt von „General Reasoning“ mit 1709, „Natural Scene Reasoning“ mit 413, „Physical Reasoning“ mit 232, „Logical Puzzle Reasoning“ mit 91 und „Chemical Reasoning“ mit 49, dem niedrigsten Wert. Die Balken sind absteigend nach Probenanzahl sortiert und zeigen eine deutliche Abnahme der Häufigkeit von links nach rechts, wobei keine Gruppierung oder Stapelung vorliegt und keine Balken visuell hervorgehoben sind.
